auth.title: Sign in to continue
auth.subtitle: D4IDE runs only for the person signed in. Sign in with GitHub or Google — the same account is used to identify your commits.
auth.deviceCodeHint: Open the GitHub page, paste the code, and approve access. This screen finishes on its own once you do.
auth.githubSetupTitle: GitHub sign-in needs a client ID (one time)
githubSetupSteps: Open GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App.
Name it D4IDE and set the homepage to https://github.com.
Enable ✓ Device Flow on the app page and save.
Copy the Client ID (not the secret) and paste it below.
auth.googleSetupTitle: Google sign-in needs a client ID (one time)
googleSetupSteps: Open Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials.
Create an OAuth client ID and choose the application type “Desktop app”.
Copy the client ID (no secret is needed) and paste it below.
The sign-in window opens in your browser and returns to the app on 127.0.0.1.
auth.privacyNote: Your sign-in token is stored encrypted on this machine with Windows DPAPI. D4IDE never sends your code or files to GitHub or Google — only the sign-in itself leaves the device.
auth.signOutHint: Signing out locks D4IDE until you sign in again.
auth.lockAppHint: With this on, the app is locked on every launch until you sign in with GitHub or Google.
auth.clientIdHint: Public client IDs only — no secrets. Used for the sign-in flows above.
auth.tokenNote: The access token is encrypted with this machine's user account and is only used to identify you.
